title: tk ask rich: multi-select, Other, async, escalate-after, tk answer
description:
Extends cmd/tk/cmd/ask.go and the v6z engine (sequenced after r6r — same files, no parallel sibling).

1. Rich shapes over the transport that already supports them: multi-select toggle keyboard + Done commit; allow_other button → ForceReply follow-up correlated back to the same pending entry. Remove the single-select fallback from r6r.
2. Async: --async registers pending + delivers + returns immediately printing the question id; tk ask --collect [--wait] gathers resolved entries as JSON lines (and with --wait blocks on the remaining ones); pending entries visible via tk list --awaiting= as today plus the pending files.
3. Escalation delay: --escalate-after <dur> sets the not-before timestamp (v6z) so local surfaces get the question immediately and Telegram only after the grace window (Peter, 2026-08-16: presence-agnostic, no presence detection).
4. tk answer <tick-id> [option-label-or-id | text]: first-class local answer verb — resolves the pending entry through the same engine path (resolved_by=terminal, note --from human), and the channel message gets edited exactly as with a phone answer. Registration in both dispatch layers + ResetFlags.
5. Stale-press hardening end-to-end: press after resolution → answerCallbackQuery "already resolved", no tick mutation (transport handles the ack; verify the engine ignores the event).

Test cases: multi-select toggle→Done → option_ids resolution; other→ForceReply reply resolves same entry; --async + --collect --wait round-trip; --escalate-after: no channel delivery before the window (fakebot asserts zero sendMessage), tk answer inside the window resolves and cancels delivery; tk answer on an option question by label and by id; stale press after tk answer → ack only.
Run: go test -short -count=1 ./internal/operator/... ./cmd/tk/...
acceptance_criteria: Rich-ask tests pass: all four shapes live end-to-end, async collect contract, escalate-after grace window proven (zero premature HTTP), tk answer symmetrical with phone answers
